# 2007 NFC Championship Game

The 2007 NFC Championship Game was the National Football Conference title game of the 2007 NFL season, played on January 20, 2008, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin, between the New York Giants and the Green Bay Packers. New York won 23–20 in overtime on a 47‑yard field goal by Lawrence Tynes after an interception of Brett Favre on the opening possession of overtime, sending the Giants to Super Bowl XLII . The game was contested in extreme cold at Lambeau Field, with wind chills around −24 °F; it has been cited as among the coldest games in NFL history and the second-coldest played at Lambeau . The broadcast on Fox drew one of the largest conference championship audiences on record, averaging 53.9 million viewers nationally (29.0/43 rating/share) . Two weeks later, the Giants defeated the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XLII .

## Background

- Venue and event identification:
 - Date: January 20, 2008 (2007 NFL season) .
 - Site: Lambeau Field, Green Bay, Wisconsin .
 - Attendance: 72,740 .
 - Referee: Terry McAulay .
- Teams:
 - Green Bay Packers: NFC North champions under head coach Mike McCarthy; starting quarterback Brett Favre .
 - New York Giants: coached by Tom Coughlin; starting quarterback Eli Manning .
- Recent head-to-head:
 - Green Bay defeated New York 35–13 at Giants Stadium on September 16, 2007, in the regular season .
- Playoff routes:
 - Green Bay entered after a Divisional Round win over the Seattle Seahawks, 42–20 .
 - New York advanced to the Super Bowl after winning the NFC Championship; subsequent postseason context is covered under “Aftermath and legacy” .

## Pre-game context and weather

Lambeau Field hosted a night game in severe cold. Multiple reliable outlets documented subzero conditions and dangerous wind chills:
- The Cap Times (Madison) reported an air temperature of −1 °F with wind chill of −24 °F and noted the game as the fifth-coldest in NFL history and second-coldest in Packers history .
- NFL.com’s “Coldest games” feature lists the matchup with a temperature of −4 °F and wind chill of −24 °F .
- NFL Films’ feature on the game (“The Chilling Championship”) emphasized that the wind chill at kickoff was −23 °F and highlighted cold-weather images circulating widely, including head coach Tom Coughlin’s frost-reddened face on the sideline .

For historical comparison at Lambeau Field, the 1967 NFL Championship (“Ice Bowl”) kicked off at −13 °F with an estimated wind chill of −36 °F, according to the National Weather Service .

## Game summary

New York controlled possession and field position early, and the teams traded the lead through the middle quarters before a tie in regulation and sudden-death overtime decided the conference title.

- First quarter:
 - The Giants opened the scoring with a 29‑yard field goal by Lawrence Tynes at 4:50 (NYG 3–0) .
- Second quarter:
 - Tynes extended New York’s lead with a 37‑yard field goal at 11:41 (NYG 6–0) .
 - Green Bay answered quickly: on the first play of the next series, Brett Favre hit Donald Driver for a 90‑yard touchdown to give the Packers a 7–6 lead at 11:18; it stood as one of the longest pass plays in NFL postseason history .
 - Mason Crosby’s 36‑yard field goal with 1:30 left in the half put Green Bay ahead 10–6 at halftime .
- Third quarter:
 - New York opened the half with a sustained drive capped by Brandon Jacobs’ 1‑yard touchdown run at 7:56 (NYG 13–10) .
 - Favre’s 12‑yard touchdown to tight end Donald Lee restored Green Bay’s lead at 5:00 (GB 17–13) .
 - The Giants responded with a ground-based march ending in Ahmad Bradshaw’s 4‑yard touchdown at 2:12 (NYG 20–17) .
- Fourth quarter:
 - Crosby tied the game 20–20 with a 37‑yard field goal at 11:46 .
 - The teams traded possessions in frigid conditions down the stretch; New York controlled the ball for a significant time-of-possession edge but did not score again in regulation .
- Overtime:
 - Winning the coin toss, Green Bay began with the ball, but on the second play of the series Brett Favre’s pass was intercepted by cornerback Corey Webster and returned to the Packers’ side of midfield, a play local coverage identified as the pivot point of the game .
 - Four plays later, Tynes converted a 47‑yard field goal at 12:25 of overtime to win 23–20 .

New York’s plan emphasized balance and possession, with the Giants holding the ball for 40:01 to Green Bay’s 22:34 and outgaining the Packers 377–264, while the defense limited the Packers to 1-of-10 on third down .

## Scoring summary

- 1st quarter
 - 4:50 — NYG: Lawrence Tynes 29‑yd FG (NYG 3–0) 
- 2nd quarter
 - 11:41 — NYG: Tynes 37‑yd FG (NYG 6–0) 
 - 11:18 — GB: Donald Driver 90‑yd pass from Brett Favre (Mason Crosby kick) (GB 7–6) 
 - 1:30 — GB: Crosby 36‑yd FG (GB 10–6) 
- 3rd quarter
 - 7:56 — NYG: Brandon Jacobs 1‑yd run (Tynes kick) (NYG 13–10) 
 - 5:00 — GB: Donald Lee 12‑yd pass from Favre (Crosby kick) (GB 17–13) 
 - 2:12 — NYG: Ahmad Bradshaw 4‑yd run (Tynes kick) (NYG 20–17) 
- 4th quarter
 - 11:46 — GB: Crosby 37‑yd FG (20–20) 
- Overtime
 - 12:25 — NYG: Tynes 47‑yd FG (NYG 23–20) 

Quarter-by-quarter: NYG 3–3–14–0–3; GB 0–10–7–3–0 .

## Statistics

Team statistics (selected):
- First downs: NYG 24; GB 13 
- Total net yards: NYG 377; GB 264 
- Yards per play: NYG 5.2; GB 5.0 
- Rushing yards: NYG 134; GB 28 
- Third-down efficiency: NYG 6/16; GB 1/10 
- Turnovers: NYG 1; GB 2 
- Penalties: NYG 6 for 50; GB 7 for 37 
- Time of possession: NYG 40:01; GB 22:34 

Individual leaders:
- Passing:
 - NYG: Eli Manning — 21/40, 251 yards, 0 TD, 0 INT (rating 72.0) 
 - GB: Brett Favre — 19/35, 236 yards, 2 TD, 2 INT (rating 70.7; long 90) 
- Rushing:
 - NYG: Brandon Jacobs — 21 carries, 67 yards, 1 TD; Ahmad Bradshaw — 16 carries, 63 yards, 1 TD 
 - GB: Ryan Grant — 13 carries, 29 yards 
- Receiving:
 - NYG: Plaxico Burress — 11 receptions, 151 yards (long 32) 
 - GB: Donald Driver — 5 receptions, 141 yards, 1 TD (long 90) 
- Defense/special teams notes:
 - Giants interceptions: Corey Webster (1 INT, 9 return yards), R.W. McQuarters (1 INT, 11 return yards) 
 - Packers sacks: A.J. Hawk (1), Kabeer Gbaja-Biamila (1) 
 - Field goals: NYG — Tynes 3/5 (long 47); GB — Crosby 2/2 (long 37) 

## Officiating

The referee was Terry McAulay . The full officiating crew, per the official flip card, was:
- Referee: Terry McAulay (77)
- Umpire: Roy Ellison (81)
- Head Linesman: Jim Mello (48)
- Line Judge: Jeff Bergman (32)
- Field Judge: Scott Steenson (88)
- Side Judge: Rick Patterson (15)
- Back Judge: Perry Paganelli (46)
- Replay Assistant: Bobby Boylston; Video Operator: David Coleman 

## Broadcast and ratings

Fox televised the game nationally . The telecast averaged 53.9 million viewers with a 29.0 rating and 43 share, according to Nielsen figures reported by industry sources; it ranked among the most-watched conference championship games on record and was the second-most watched sporting event in the United States in 2008 after Super Bowl XLII .

## Significance, aftermath, and legacy

- Overtime and Favre’s final Packers appearance:
 - The game was decided on Lawrence Tynes’ 47‑yard field goal in overtime, set up by Corey Webster’s interception of Brett Favre’s pass on the second play of the extra session .
 - Local coverage noted this was Favre’s final game in a Packers uniform before his subsequent departure from Green Bay, a point widely cited in retrospectives of his career .
- Super Bowl implications:
 - The Giants advanced to Super Bowl XLII, where they defeated the previously unbeaten New England Patriots 17–14 .
- Cold-weather legacy:
 - The contest has been highlighted by NFL Films among the league’s “100 Greatest Games,” in part for its extreme conditions; NFL.com and other outlets have characterized it among the coldest games in NFL history and the second-coldest at Lambeau Field, trailing the 1967 “Ice Bowl” .
- Individual and team narratives:
 - Plaxico Burress’ 11‑catch, 151‑yard performance became one of the defining efforts of the Giants’ postseason run .
 - The 90‑yard Favre-to-Driver touchdown is listed among the longest pass plays in NFL postseason history .

## Records and notable feats

- Longest pass plays (postseason context): Brett Favre’s 90‑yard touchdown to Donald Driver ranks among the longest pass plays in NFL playoff history .
- Cold-weather context:
 - NFL.com places the game among the league’s coldest, listing a −24 °F wind chill; Cap Times reported −1 °F air temperature with −24 °F wind chill and described it as the fifth-coldest game in NFL history and the second-coldest in Packers history .
 - By comparison, the 1967 “Ice Bowl” at Lambeau began at −13 °F with an estimated −36 °F wind chill, per the National Weather Service .

## Box/score data sources

Official and authoritative statistical records for scoring chronology, team and individual statistics, and play details (including drive times) are documented in Pro‑Football‑Reference’s game page and ESPN’s box score/game page , with officiating crew corroborated by the Pro Football Hall of Fame flip card .

### Loss: Packers 20, N.Y. Giants 23 OT (NFC Championship)

![Image 15: FavreRetires-49.jpg](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

Brett Favre rushes off the field after losing to the Giants 23-20 in frigid conditions at Lambeau Field. The Green Bay Packers hosted the New York Giants in the NFC Championship game Sunday Jan. 20, 2008.

Steve Apps - State Journal archives

Fifth coldest game in NFL history, second coldest in Packers history.

**Date:**Jan. 20, 2008

**Temperature:**-1 degree (wind chill: -24 degrees)

**Stadium:**Lambeau Field

**Attendance:**72,740

**Coach:**Mike McCarthy

**Starting QB:**Brett Favre

**Regular season record:**13-3-0, .813, 1st in NFC North

**Game notes:** Brett Favre threw an interception in overtime to set up the Giants' game-winning field goal. The game was Favre's last in a Packers uniform.

8.title: QnJldHQgRmF2cmU6IE1lbW9yYWJsZSBtb21lbnRz
8.content:
Published: May 29, 2008 at 01:31 PM

Some of the most memorable moments from the 17-year career of Brett Favre:

» **Sept. 13, 1992, at Tampa Bay.** Favre completes his first NFL pass -- to himself. A deflected pass lands in Favre's hands, and he is tackled for a 7-yard loss. Favre completes eight of 14 passes for 73 yards.

» **Sept. 20, 1992, vs. Cincinnati at Lambeau Field.** Replaces injured starter Don Majkowski in the first quarter, and never looks back. Favre leads two scoring drives in the final eight minutes of the game. His 35-yard touchdown pass to Kitrick Taylor with 13 seconds remaining gives the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) a come-from-behind 24-23 victory over the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://www.nfl.com/teams/cincinnatibengals/profile?team=CIN).

» **Nov. 15, 1992, vs. Philadelphia in Milwaukee.** Despite sustaining a first-degree separation of his left shoulder early in the game, Favre leads the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) to a come-from-behind 27-24 victory. Reggie White, then a defensive end for the [Eagles](https://www.nfl.com/teams/philadelphiaeagles/profile?team=PHI), would later say the toughness Favre showed was a factor in his decision to sign with Green Bay as a free agent in the offseason.

» **Jan. 8, 1994, at Detroit.** With the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) trailing 24-21 in the final minute of a Wild Card playoff game, Favre rolls to his left and throws across his body, completing a 40-yard pass to Sterling Sharpe on the other side of the field with 55 seconds remaining to give the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) a 28-24 victory.

» **Oct. 31, 1994, at Chicago.** Playing with a severely bruised hip in a driving rainstorm at Soldier Field, Favre rushes for a career-high 58 yards -- including a 36-yard touchdown in the second quarter when Favre leaped over a [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) defender -- and leads the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) to a 33-6 victory.

» **Dec. 18, 1994, vs. Atlanta in Milwaukee.** With the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) needing a victory to keep their playoff chances alive, Favre's diving 9-yard touchdown run with 14 seconds left gives the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) a 21-17 victory over the [Falcons](https://www.nfl.com/teams/atlantafalcons/profile?team=ATL) in the final football game at County Stadium.

» **Sept. 11, 1995, at Chicago.** Favre throws a 99-yard touchdown pass to Robert Brooks -- becoming only the eighth QB in league history to do so -- and the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) beat the [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) 27-24.

» **Nov. 12, 1995, vs. Chicago at Lambeau.** Playing with a severely sprained left ankle that forced him to the bench in the previous week's game at Minnesota and would eventually require offseason surgery, Favre throws five touchdown passes in a 35-28 victory over the [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI).

» **Dec. 24, 1995, vs. Pittsburgh at Lambeau.** Favre rolls out and is hit hard by three [Steelers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/pittsburghsteelers/profile?team=PIT) defenders, forcing the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) to call timeout and sending Favre to the sidelines coughing up blood. He returns to throw a 1-yard touchdown pass to Mark Chmura on the next play. The [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB)' 24-19 victory clinches the division title.

» **Jan. 6, 1996, at San Francisco.** Favre completes 21 of 28 passes for 299 yards and two touchdowns as the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) knock the defending [Super Bowl](http://www.nfl.com/superbowl/47) champion [49ers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/sanfrancisco49ers/profile?team=SF) out of the playoffs with a 27-17 victory.

» **Jan. 4, 1997, vs. San Francisco at Lambeau.** Playing in rough weather conditions, Favre completes only 11 of 15 passes for 79 yards, but the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) roll to a 35-14 playoff victory over the [49ers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/sanfrancisco49ers/profile?team=SF).

**» Jan. 12, 1997, vs. Carolina at Lambeau Field.** Favre is 19-of-29 for 292 yards in the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB)' NFC Championship game victory over the [Panthers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/carolinapanthers/profile?team=CAR), 30-13.

» **Jan. 26, 1997.** In [Super Bowl](http://www.nfl.com/superbowl/47) XXXI at the Louisiana Superdome, Favre is 14-of-27 for 246 yards and no interceptions to beat the [New England Patriots](https://www.nfl.com/teams/newenglandpatriots/profile?team=NE) 35-21 -- the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB)' first championship in 29 years. Favre throws a 54-yard touchdown pass to Andre Rison on his first throw of the game. Later, he throws a [Super Bowl](http://www.nfl.com/superbowl/47)\-record 81-yard touchdown pass to Antonio Freeman.

» **Jan. 11, 1998, at San Francisco.** Trudging through the mud in sloppy San Francisco, Favre is 16-of-27 for 222 yards and a touchdown as the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) beat the [49ers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/sanfrancisco49ers/profile?team=SF) 23-10 to advance to the [Super Bowl](http://www.nfl.com/superbowl/47) for the second straight season, where they lose to the [Denver Broncos](https://www.nfl.com/teams/denverbroncos/profile?team=DEN) 31-24.

» **[Dec. 3, 2001, at Jacksonville.](https://www.nfl.com/gamecenter?game_id=17857&displayPage=tab_gamecenter&season=2001&week=REG12)** Favre throws for 362 yards and three touchdowns, but wins with his feet. Favre's 6-yard touchdown run with 1:30 remaining -- his first rushing touchdown in three years -- gives the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) a come-from-behind 28-21 victory.

» **[Jan. 4, 2004, at Lambeau.](https://www.nfl.com/gamecenter?game_id=26643&displayPage=tab_gamecenter&season=2003&week=POST18)** Favre throws for 319 yards to get the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) to overtime, and Seattle quarterback [Matt Hasselbeck](https://www.nfl.com/player/matthasselbeck/2501078/profile) -- Favre's former understudy -- proclaims after the coin flip that "We want the ball and we're gonna score!" They don't. Hasselbeck throws an interception that is returned for a touchdown and the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) win 33-27 in overtime.

» **[Dec. 31, 2006, at Chicago.](https://www.nfl.com/gamecenter?game_id=29112&displayPage=tab_gamecenter&season=2006&week=REG17)** Favre throws for 285 yards and a touchdown in a 26-7 victory over the [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI), the No. 1 playoff seed in the NFC. Favre gets choked up in a television interview after the game, leading some to believe he had played his final game. But after once again mulling retirement, he decides to return.

» **[Oct. 29, 2007 at Denver.](https://www.nfl.com/gamecenter?game_id=29310&displayPage=tab_gamecenter&season=2007&week=REG8)** Favre throws an 82-yard touchdown to Greg Jennings on the first play from scrimmage in overtime, leading the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) to a 19-13 victory.

» **[Jan. 20, 2008 vs. New York Giants at Lambeau.](https://www.nfl.com/gamecenter?game_id=29525&displayPage=tab_gamecenter&season=2007&week=POST20)** Aside from a 90-yard touchdown to wide receiver Donald Driver, Favre generally struggles in subzero temperatures in the NFC Championship game. His interception in overtime sets up the [Giants](https://www.nfl.com/teams/newyorkgiants/profile?team=NYG)' game-winning field goal, and the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) lose 23-20.

=============================================

The Saints’ march to the Super Bowl attracted the largest non-Super Bowl TV audience in nearly 12 years.

Sunday’s Vikings/Saints NFC Championship Game drew a massive 30.6/45 fast-national rating and 57.9 million viewers on FOX, up 39% in ratings and 43% in viewers from Ravens/Steelers on CBS last year (22.0/34, 40.6 mil), and up 5% and 7%, respectively, from Giants/Packers on FOX in ’08 (29.0/43, 53.9 mil).

The game peaked with a 34.4/48 rating and 65.2 million viewers from 9:30-10 PM.

Vikings/Saints stands as the second-most viewed Conference Championship game in NFL history, behind only the 1982 Cowboys/49ers NFC title game on CBS (68.7 mil).

Additionally, the 30.6/45 rating is the highest for a Conference Championship game since Packers/Cowboys in ’96 (33.3/58).

To put the numbers in perspective, no World Series game has drawn a rating of 30.6 or higher since Braves/Twins Game 7 in ’91 (32.2/49), and no NBA Finals game has ever drawn a rating that high.

Vikings/Saints also drew a higher rating than every single primetime Olympics telecast — Summer or Winter — since ’94. That includes the ’96 Atlanta and ’02 Salt Lake City games.

Excluding the Super Bowl, the game ranks as the most-viewed television program on any network since the series finale of Seinfeld in ’98 (76.3 mil) — topping the previous 12-year high of 53.9 million for Giants/Packers in ’08 — and the most-viewed program in the history of the FOX network.

Overall, FOX averaged a 22.4/38 rating and 40.2 million viewers for its coverage of the NFL playoffs — the network’s highest rated postseason since ’97 and most-viewed ever.

**50th Anniversary of the Ice Bowl: December 31, 1967**

The 1967 NFL Championship Game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Green Bay Packers, played on December 31 at Lambeau Field, is known as the Ice Bowl, arguably one of the greatest games in NFL history.

The game was played in brutal cold and windy conditions. The kickoff temperature in Green Bay was -13**°**F, with a wind chill of 36 below zero. Temperatures were so cold, in fact, that referees had to shout signals so that the metal whistles wouldn't stick to their lips. Even so, nearly 51,000 fans watched the coldest game in league annals.

Several players were treated for frostbite and a fan in the stands died of exposure to the cold.

Bart Starr, the Green Bay Packers Hall of Fame quarterback, scored the game-winning touchdown with 13 seconds remaining, clinching a third straight NFL Championship for the Packers.![Image 4: A black and white photograph of the Green Bay Packers and Dallas Cowboys in the 1967 NFL Championship Game, also known as the Ice Bowl, played on December 31, 1967, at Lambeau Field](http://www.weather.gov/images/grb/events/123167/ice-bowl-3.jpg)

Green Bay Packers quarterback Bart Starr scores the game-winning touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys in the NFL Championship Game on Dec. 31, 1967, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay._(AP Photo)_

*   **[Green Bay - Ice Bowl Weather Facts](https://www.weather.gov/grb/123167_Icebowl#wind)**
*   **[Weather Leading Up to the Ice Bowl](https://www.weather.gov/grb/123167_Icebowl#hydro)**
*   **[Weather the Day of the Ice Bowl](https://www.weather.gov/grb/123167_Icebowl#snow)**

Green Bay - Ice Bowl Weather Facts

*   The coldest and longest cold stretch (nine days) during the 1967-1968 winter season began the day of the Ice Bowl. Seven of nine days during that stretch did not exceed 0**°**F.
*   The winter in which the Ice Bowl was played (1967-1968) ranked 2nd all-time for the least snowiest (20.6 inches). The record is 19.2 inches during the winter of 1960-1961.
*   The Ice Bowl ranked 1st all-time for the lowest average temperature for any December 31 in Green Bay: -6.5**°**F for the day.
*   The Ice Bowl ranked 1st all-time for the lowest minimum temperature for any December 31 in Green Bay: -19**°**F reached just before midnight that evening.
*   The Ice Bowl ranked 5th all-time for the lowest maximum temperature for any December 31 in Green Bay: +6**°**F reached at midnight early that morning.

* * *

The Weather Leading Up to the Ice Bowl

The overall weather pattern during the month of December 1967 underwent a rather dramatic "second half adjustment." The upper level flow during the first half of the month was characterized by a "split flow" regime.The west-to-east northern stream over Canada essentially blocked the Arctic air from moving southward into the United States (figure on left, below).However, during the second half of the month, the upper air pattern changed dramatically such that by the end of December 1967, a large polar vortex had become established over Hudson Bay with a large and deep trough centered right over the central United States (figure on right, below).This pattern change allowed the Arctic air that was building up in Canada earlier in the month to spill south into the United States by the end of the month.

![Image 5: Upper air chart for December 16, 1967](http://www.weather.gov/images/grb/events/123167/ua1.png)![Image 6: Upper air chart for December 28, 1967](http://www.weather.gov/images/grb/events/123167/ua2.png)
500 mb (~ 18000 ft) chart on December 16, 1967._Click image for larger view._ 500 mb (~ 18000 ft) chart on December 28, 1967._Click image for larger view._

The graph below shows the trend in the daily average temperature during the month of December 1967.

![Image 7: December 1967 daily average temperatures](http://www.weather.gov/images/grb/events/123167/temp1.png)
Daily average temperatures in December 1967._Click image for larger view._

* * *

The Weather the Day of the Ice Bowl

The weather the day before the Ice Bowl was relatively tranquil with a high of 20**°**F.However, later that evening shortly before midnight, an Arctic front swept across the state ushering bitter cold air into the state. The temperature fell nearly 30 degrees during the 12 hour period ending at 9 AM the morning of the Ice Bowl.By 9 AM Sunday, December 31, 1967, the temperature plummeted to minus 16**°**F with wind chill values falling to 38 below zero.During the game, actual temperatures ranged from -12**°**F to -14**°**F with wind chills (based on the new wind chill index) ranging from 33 to 37 below zero, making it the coldest game in NFL history.

Surface weather chart on December 31, 1967._Click image for larger view._ Three-hourly weather on December 31, 1967._Click image for larger view._
